title: frameledger survey --json
description: The result of `frameledger survey FILE... --json`: many runs against one frame budget. A later release may add keys, and values to the open sets; a script ignores what it does not know. Print this file from the same frameledger that printed the result.

frameledger.description: The version of the frameledger that printed this.

summary.description: The opening sentences of the text output, in order. Wording may change in any release.

overrides.description: The --override flags given; empty for a command that takes none.

warnings.description: The warnings, each also a sentence in summary.

run_id.description: The header's run_id; null for a file that could not be read.

reason.description: Why the run is unjudged or inconclusive, when there is a reason to give; null otherwise.

rank.description: Its place among the runs, worst first, from 1; null when it is not ranked.

worst_kind.description: The segment kind the run is ranked by; null with no rank, and for frames with no segment.

worst_segment.description: The worst segment of that kind; null with no rank, and for frames with no segment.

median_ms.description: The worst kind's median frame/wall, in ms; null with no rank.

p99_ms.description: The worst kind's 99th percentile frame/wall, in ms; null with no rank.

frames_over_budget.description: How many judged frames are over the budget; null for a run that could not be judged.

top_pass.description: category/name of the frame's largest depth-0 cpu or gpu cost, a remainder included; null when the frame has none, as in an imported run.

slowest_over.description: The slowest frame over the budget; null when no judged frame is over it.

segment_kind.description: The segment's kind, the part of a segment name before its colon; an engine chooses its kinds, such as view or spot. Null for frames with no segment.

ranked.description: Whether the kind has enough frames to rank the run by.

kinds.description: The run's figures per segment kind.

generated_frames.description: How many of the run's frames a frame generator made; null for a file that could not be read.

runs.description: Each file, in rank order, then the unranked in the order given.

warmup_s.description: --warmup-s: the seconds left out at the start of each run.

allowed.description: --allow-frames: how many frames of a run may be over the budget.

all_frames.description: Whether --all-frames counted the frames a frame generator made.

survey_verdict.description: The verdict of survey: fail when a run is flagged, inconclusive when none is but a run is unjudged or inconclusive, pass when every run is judged and none is flagged. A closed set.

survey_exit_code.description: The exit codes the result of survey can carry. A closed set.

code.description: What kind of warning it is. An open set: a later release may add a code, and a script ignores one it does not know. file_error says a file could not be read.

warning.description: One warning. Its sentence is also in summary.

field.description: The header field that may differ.

override.description: One blocking field a --override flag let differ.

survey_run_verdict.description: What became of one run: flagged when it is over the budget, clean, inconclusive, or unjudged when it could not be judged. A closed set.
